title: edikt hook corpus matrix (ADR-063 Decision §2/§3)
description: One file per hook at test/fixtures/hook-corpus/<hook>/matrix.yaml, hand-curated (ADR-063: 'the hand-work is matrix curation, not expectation authoring'). Each scenario names which of the four axes it exercises (payload / config / environment / ordering); the recorder (SR-009) executes every scenario against the current bash hook (the living oracle) and writes a recording (hook-corpus-recording.v1) for it. A hook's coverage-gap table (AC-002-2) is this file's scenario list cross-referenced against the four axes — a hook with zero scenarios tagged 'ordering' has an open ordering-axis gap, visible directly from this file without re-deriving it.

hook.description: MUST match a hook-registry.v1 row's name.

id.description: Stable scenario id — becomes the recording directory name, so it MUST NOT be renumbered once recorded (a rename orphans the prior recording rather than superseding it).

axis.description: Which of ADR-063 Decision §2's four axes this scenario exercises. A scenario MAY tag more than one axis (e.g. an ordering scenario also varies payload across its steps).

source_finding.description: Optional provenance back-reference for a scenario that reproduces a specific measured finding — e.g. F-041 (spaced file_path), F-036 (exit-code semantics), F-074 (side-effect-only observable). Not required for every scenario, but every hook's matrix for which F-041/F-036/F-074 applies MUST carry at least one scenario citing it (SAC — see spec.md).

payload.description: Relative path to a JSON payload fixture (may point into the existing test/fixtures/hook-payloads/ tree, or a hook-corpus-local payload for a class the existing tree has no fixture for — e.g. F-041's spaced path). Null when the hook takes no stdin payload (a library scenario, or a hook exercised with no input) — ignored when sequence is set.

config.description: Relative path to a .edikt/config.yaml fixture, or the literal "default" for the project's own committed config. Ignored when sequence is set.

env.description: Environment variable overrides for this scenario. A null value means the variable is explicitly unset (removed from the recorder's subprocess environment) rather than left at whatever the harness process happens to have — the environment axis requires presence/absence to be a deliberate, recorded fact, not an accident of the invoking shell. Ignored when sequence is set.

sequence.description: Present only for a call-ordering-axis scenario (dedup TTL windows, ADR-050's duplicate-invocation class). Each step is a full sub-invocation, executed against the SAME sandbox tree in order, with the tree state carried forward between steps — the point of the axis is that step 2 observes step 1's filesystem effects.

delay_ms.description: Optional simulated gap before this step, for a dedup-TTL scenario whose outcome depends on elapsed time. The recorder MUST NOT sleep wall-clock for this — see spec.md Testing Strategy for the clock-injection approach.

notes.description: Free-text rationale for why this scenario exists — required in practice by review discipline, not by the schema, since a scenario with no stated reason is the next one deleted by an editor who cannot tell if it is load-bearing.
